title: Article 328 — Power of Legislature of a State to make provision with respect to elections to such Legislature

content.overview: Article 328 provides that subject to the provisions of the Constitution and so far as provision in that behalf is not made by Parliament, the Legislature of a State may from time to time by law make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, the elections to the House or either House of the Legislature of the State, including the preparation of electoral rolls and all other matters necessary for securing the due constitution of such House or Houses.
content.glance: State Legislature may make election law for its own House(s) only where Parliament has not provided, and subject to the Constitution.
content.study:
Article 328 is a residual/supplemental State power:
- Subject to the Constitution.
- Only so far as provision is not made by Parliament.
- Matters relating to elections to the State Legislature (including rolls and due constitution).

Parliamentary law under Article 327 prevails in the field it occupies.

Examination: subordinate to Constitution and parliamentary law; State Legislature elections only.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Subject to the Constitution and so far as Parliament has not provided, a State Legislature may by law provide for matters relating to elections to its own House or Houses.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What power does a State Legislature have under Article 328?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 328, subject to the provisions of the Constitution and so far as provision in that behalf is not made by Parliament, the Legislature of a State may from time to time by law make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, the elections to the House or either House of the Legislature of the State, including the preparation of electoral rolls and all other matters necessary for securing the due constitution of such House or Houses.

examTips: Residual State power; subject to Constitution and parliamentary law.

keyTakeaways: Art 328: residual State power over elections to its own Legislature.
